* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and west central New Mexico,
including the following areas, in north central New Mexico, Far
Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains and Northwest Highlands. In
west central New Mexico, West Central Highlands and West Central
Mountains.

moving north over the region through the predawn hours before
tapering off around sunrise. Another 1 inch of rainfall on

will redevelop Friday afternoon. Rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches
per hour are possible.

properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:47PM MST until October 23 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues in Oak
Creek.

* WHERE...Oak Creek in Coconino and Yavapai counties...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Oak Creek is occurring. Deadly flooding over
low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1144 PM MST, a river gauges on Oak Creek showed falling water
levels, however the flow remained elevated and near action stage.
Water levels are expected to gradually fall through the overnight
and into Friday morning.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Dry Creek, Pumphouse Wash, West Fork Oak Creek, Spring Creek,
Verde River, Oak Creek and Turkey Creek.
- For Oak Creek at Cornville:
At 11:00pm the stage was 6.27 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park
upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge.
At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of
Page Springs Road Bridge.

- For Oak Creek at Oak Creek at Sedona:
At 10:45pm the stage was 6.29 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges
over Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable.
At 7.0 feet: Likely to cause minor flooding downstream in Page
Springs area 4 to 6 hours later.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sedona, Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs, Indian Gardens, Pine
Flats, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State Park, Slide Rock State Park,
West Fork of Oak Creek, Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness,
Cathedral Rock, East Pocket Lookout Tower and Oak Creek Vista
Overlook.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Manzanita Campground, Pine Flat Campground, Cave Springs
Campground and Windmill Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Pumphouse Wash, Slide Rock, Encinoso, Grasshopper Point, Midgely
Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing", Crescent Moon Ranch and
Mormons Crossing.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
